moduleDoc:
Tool surfaces for the code arms, served to an agent loop through MCP.

Two arms, one contract.  Each is a tiny toolkit (``get_tools_spec`` /
``execute_tool``) that an MCP server can expose to Codex:

* ``cells``  - one tool ``python(code)``: the code runs in a *persistent*
  namespace where ``robo`` lives, like a notebook or OpenAI's python tool.
  Variables and functions defined in one cell are available in the next.
* ``program`` - one tool ``run_program(code | path)``: the code is a complete
  file defining ``run(robo)``; every program starts from a fresh namespace
  (files in the workspace persist and can be imported).  ``max_programs=1``
  is the single-shot protocol.

Both arms also get ``finish(status, summary)``.  Every tool result is text
(stdout, errors, the ledger of primitive calls, the robot state) plus the two
current camera images whenever the robot moved, so the agent's per-turn
perception matches what a tool-calling agent receives after each primitive.

moduleDoc:
Drive one code-arm episode with Claude Code through the Claude Agent SDK.

The second agent runtime of :mod:`pyrualean.play` (``--runtime claude``).
Everything around the agent loop is the Codex runtime's: the same HTTP MCP
server over :class:`~pyrualean.arms.ArmToolkit`, the same prompt text and
step-0 card images.  Claude Code owns the loop (``claude_agent_sdk.query``)
and keeps its default system prompt, as RPent's Claude planner does: our
prompt is the first user message, the card images ride along as base64
image blocks.  This module owns the wall clock, the event dump
(``claude_events.jsonl``) and the usage audit that becomes
``result["generation"]``.

symbols.doc:
Token usage in the Codex audit's vocabulary.

One assistant message id is one model request.  Per request only the
prompt side is trustworthy: the CLI stamps every assistant message
with the request's ``message_start`` usage, whose ``output_tokens``
is a streaming placeholder.  The run totals come from the result
message (verified on Claude Code 2.1.280: its top-level ``usage``
sums the main model's requests, while ``usage.iterations`` holds a
single entry for a whole tool loop, so it is ignored).  Without a
result (timeout, crash) the prompt sums are rebuilt from the
assistant messages and the output side is reported as unknown.
symbols.body:
entries = [self.requests[k] for k in self.request_order]
per_request = [_prompt_tokens(u) for u in entries]
profile: list[int] = []
for tokens in per_request:
            profile.append(profile[-1] + tokens if profile else tokens)
out: dict[str, Any] = {"requests": len(self.request_order), "request_profile": profile}
result_usage = getattr(self.result, "usage", None)
if isinstance(result_usage, dict) and result_usage:
            out["input_tokens"] = _prompt_tokens(result_usage)
            out["cached_input_tokens"] = _int(result_usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens"))
out["total_tokens"] = (
            out["input_tokens"] + out["output_tokens"] if out["output_tokens"] is not None else None
        )
return out

Tracing interrupts Python loops in policy/workspace frames, including helpers

In-process streamable-HTTP MCP server over an :class:`ArmToolkit`.

Adapted from RPent's ``HttpMcpServer`` (same wire behaviour: a lowlevel MCP
``Server`` served by uvicorn on a background thread) with two differences:
it does not import RPent, and every tool is published with MCP annotations
so an agent runtime can apply its tool-approval policy without a human or a
reviewer model in the loop.

from mcp import types
blocks = getattr(result, "content_blocks", None)
if blocks is None:
        return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=str(result))], False
out: list[Any] = []
for block in blocks:
        if block.get("type") == "text":
            out.append(types.TextContent(type="text", text=block.get("text", "")))
payload = getattr(result, "result", None)
is_error = isinstance(payload, dict) and result_is_error(payload)
return out, is_error

moduleDoc:
A plain OpenAI chat-completions agent loop for the code arms (``--runtime openai``).

The Codex and Claude runtimes hand the agent loop to a coding-agent product
with its own system prompt, tools and transcript format.  This runtime is the
third option: the loop lives here, talks to *any* OpenAI-compatible
``/v1/chat/completions`` endpoint (a gateway, a local SGLang / vLLM server, a
training framework's rollout engine) with function calling, and executes the
arm's tools in-process through :class:`pyrualean.arms.ArmToolkit` (no MCP
server, no subprocess).  It is what a small open model, a distillation
teacher and an RL rollout all share.

Protocol (one episode):

1. The first user message carries the full prompt text and the task card
   images as ``image_url`` data URIs (same content Codex / Claude get).
2. Each assistant reply may carry ``tool_calls``; they are executed in order
   through ``ArmToolkit.execute_tool`` and answered with one ``tool`` message
   each.  Images returned by a tool (``on-motion`` or ``robo.show()``) cannot
   travel in a ``tool`` message under the OpenAI schema, so they follow in one
   extra ``user`` message that names the tool call they belong to.
3. The episode ends when the agent calls ``finish``, when it replies without
   a tool call (after ``nudges`` reminders), when the decision budget is
   spent (``ArmToolkit`` refuses further ``python`` calls), when the wall
   clock ``budget_s`` runs out, or when the provider keeps failing.

Everything the model saw and said is written to ``messages.json`` (images
replaced by references to PNG files under ``images/``), every request to
``openai_events.jsonl``, and the usual ``generation`` record (Codex's token
conventions: ``input_tokens`` includes cached tokens) goes into
``result.json`` by :mod:`pyrualean.play`.

symbols.name: _resize_png
symbols.doc: Downscale ``data`` so its longer side is ``max_side``; returns (png, scale).
symbols.body:
if not max_side:
        return data, 1.0
from PIL import Image
image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(data))
longest = max(image.size)
if longest <= max_side:
        return data, 1.0
scale = max_side / longest
resized = image.resize(
        (max(1, round(image.width * scale)), max(1, round(image.height * scale)))
    )
buffer = io.BytesIO()
resized.save(buffer, format="PNG")
return buffer.getvalue(), scale

A cell can loop over primitives for minutes; this loop *is* the host thread, so without a
timer the wall-clock budget would only be noticed after the cell returned (the Codex and
Claude runtimes stop the robot from the host while the agent process keeps running).  The
timer fires ``on_timeout``, which makes the next primitive raise ``EpisodeFinished``.

Run one episode's agent loop; returns the ``generation`` record.

``status`` is ``completed`` (the agent finished, stopped calling tools, or
spent its decision budget), ``timeout`` (``budget_s`` expired:
``on_timeout`` is called first) or ``error`` (the provider failed after
``retries``); ``returncode`` mirrors the Claude runtime: 0 clean, 2 after
a provider error, ``None`` on timeout.  ``extra_body`` is merged into
every request (``reasoning_effort``, ``chat_template_kwargs`` ...).
``tool_choice`` is OpenAI's: ``auto`` lets the model answer in text,
``required`` makes every reply a tool call (``python`` or ``finish``),
which small thinking models need (they otherwise think and emit nothing).
``image_max_side`` downscales every image the model receives (0 keeps the
native 1024 px that the prompt's pixel coordinates refer to).
``should_stop`` is asked between requests, between retries and during a rate
limit's wait: once it answers true the loop ends there (``completed``) without
another request.  It is how a host says that whoever owns the environment has
ended the episode, so that nothing the model could still write would count.

moduleDoc:
Drive one episode of a code arm with an agent runtime: Codex, Claude Code or OpenAI.

The host boots RPent's stack for the chosen robot (``--robot``), wraps it in
the adapter's robot class (:class:`LiberoRobot` for LIBERO),
exposes the arm's tools (``python`` / ``run_program`` + ``finish``) through
RPent's in-process HTTP MCP server and launches the agent against it:
``codex exec`` (``--runtime codex``, the default), Claude Code through the
Claude Agent SDK (``--runtime claude``, :mod:`pyrualean.claude_runtime`), or
an in-process chat-completions loop against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
(``--runtime openai``, :mod:`pyrualean.openai_runtime`: the arm's tools are
called directly, no MCP server is needed by the agent).
The runtime owns the agent loop; this module owns the budget, the audit of
the event stream and ``result.json``.  One episode per process.

symbols.name: _agent_environment
symbols.doc:
Build a minimal, leak-free environment for the agent process.

Codex: the sandbox shell Codex gives the model is a login shell; it must
not inherit ``ZDOTDIR``/``CODEX_HOME*`` pointers to other Codex homes
(whose memories the model would otherwise read) nor the launcher's own
session variables.  ``SHELL`` is pinned to bash so the user's zsh profile
is not sourced inside the sandbox.

Claude: the same allow-list plus :data:`_CLAUDE_ENV_KEEP`.  The Claude
Agent SDK merges this dict *over* the launcher's environment when it
spawns ``claude`` (it cannot withhold variables), so the list is the
explicit contract of what the runtime needs; the agent gets no shell
there, so nothing else can be discovered through it.

symbols.name: _usage_from_rollouts
symbols.doc:
Recover cumulative token usage from Codex's session rollout files.

``codex exec --json`` only reports usage on ``turn.completed``; a session
that was killed at the budget never emits it.  The rollout Codex keeps
under ``$CODEX_HOME/sessions`` records a ``token_count`` event after every
model response, so the last one gives the total for the thread.

symbols.name: _codex_context_config
symbols.doc:
Effective context-window and auto-compaction settings of the agent.

Codex applies ``$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`` first and ``-c`` overrides on
top; :func:`_codex_argv` only passes ``model_auto_compact_token_limit``
when ``CODEX_AUTO_COMPACT_TOKEN_LIMIT`` is set, so the value in the home's
``config.toml`` is what governs a run otherwise.  Recorded in
``result.json`` because compaction changes what the model sees.

symbols.name: play_episode
symbols.doc:
Run one episode of ``arm`` on ``cell`` and write ``result.json``.

``robot`` selects the adapter (robot class, host module, knowledge);
``cell`` is that host's ``Cell`` and ``boot_options`` its ``boot``
keyword arguments (shared servers, model paths).  ``primitives`` is the
primitive set the policy may use (``full`` or ``no-vla``: the robot's VLA
primitives are hidden from the prompt and refused at call time; the
servers boot as usual); ``result.json`` records it as
``host.primitive_set``.

``runtime`` picks the agent: ``codex`` runs ``codex exec`` in a
subprocess, ``claude`` runs Claude Code through the Claude Agent SDK
(:func:`pyrualean.claude_runtime.run_claude_agent`; ``claude_cli`` names
the ``claude`` executable, the SDK's bundled one when it cannot be
found), ``openai`` runs :func:`pyrualean.openai_runtime.run_openai_agent`
in-process against ``base_url`` (the key read from ``api_key_env``;
``openai_options`` are its keyword arguments: ``temperature``,
``max_tokens``, ``extra_body``, ``image_max_side``, ``nudges`` ...).
Boot, prompt, MCP server, budgets and ``result.json`` are the same for
all; only the event stream files (``<runtime>_events.jsonl``,
``<runtime>_stderr.txt``) and ``generation`` are runtime-specific.

``codex_home`` points Codex at a clean ``CODEX_HOME`` (no memories, no
history) so nothing from earlier sessions leaks into the episode.
``guides=True`` copies the robot's operating guides (LIBERO's three by
default) into ``workspace/guides/`` and tells the agent they are there;
``guides_dir`` names the directory (default: the adapter's guides under
RPent's checkout).  ``max_turns`` switches the episode to a decision
budget: at most that many tool calls, ``budget_s`` then being only a
safety ceiling that the prompt does not mention.

symbols.doc: Keyword arguments of :func:`run_openai_agent` from the ``openai runtime`` flags.

moduleDoc:
Small feedback loops extracted from the RSI relocalization/correction pattern.

These helpers contain no task geometry or robot-specific primitive calls.
Callbacks use the current robot's public API. Exceptions and host pauses
propagate to the outer model loop; no helper replays a failed code block.

symbols.name: _verdict
verify_grasp
symbols.doc:
Close, test support with one small probe, then verify fresh paired evidence.

close(attempt) returns the controller result; probe(closed, attempt) performs
one bounded, safe diagnostic movement. observe() returns GraspObservation.
compare(closed, after) checks whether the intended object followed the
gripper and stayed stable relative to it, using permitted before/after data.
It returns bool/None. A fresh object_held=True is also required to verify.

Only a definite failed grasp can use repair(observation, next_attempt).
Fresh contact can permit a small probe while visual support is unknown.
Unresolved support after the probe, stale evidence and refused motion exit
without repair.
Optional allow_action(kind, attempt) must return bool and is checked before
close/probe/repair, e.g. to reserve steps/time for handover and insertion.
Callbacks must bound their own primitive costs; this is not a motion planner
or a replacement for host timeouts, watch contracts and phase prerequisites.
Exceptions and supervision pauses propagate without automatic replay.

symbols.name: relocalize
symbols.doc:
Observe up to max_attempts times; optionally change view between reads.

observe() returns a NEW observation. valid(observation) must return bool
or None (unknown). prepare_view(previous, attempt) runs before each repeat
read, with attempt starting at 1. It may clear occlusion or select another
camera. Callers must check status before using the returned observation.

symbols.name: correct
symbols.doc:
Bounded correction or grasp attempts, verified after EVERY attempt.

observe() reads current evidence; complete(observation) returns bool/None.
act(observation, attempt) performs one bounded correction (attempt starts
at 1). error(observation), when supplied, is a finite nonnegative residual
in caller-defined units. Stop after no_progress_limit insufficient
improvements. Unknown completion hands control back without another act.
A holding predicate must establish the intended object, not just closure.
